title: A feathered fossil
hook: A fossil may preserve an outline beyond the bones.

knows: Some fossils preserve traces of soft structures.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish evidence of feathers from proof of powered flight.

misconception: Any feathered dinosaur must have been capable of powered flight.
objective: Distinguish evidence of feathers from proof of powered flight.

claims.text: A fossil may preserve an outline beyond the bones. A non-avian dinosaur fossil preserves feather impressions. What does this evidence alone establish about powered flight? The illustrated fossil includes a feather impression. Feathers can have functions besides powered flight, so their presence alone does not prove that this animal flew. The schematic does not establish the actual function of the feathers.

claims.text: The figure is a simplified, not-to-scale schematic of a stated example, not an image of an identified specimen.
Recall: A fossil preserves feather impressions but no other evidence of flight. What can be concluded? The presence of feathers does not by itself establish powered flight.
